status: DRAFT v0.1: not yet reviewed, pretested or calibrated.
notes: High pole is consistently 'more restriction / more paternalism'. This domain tests whether a personal-liberty axis exists separately from G, which compass-style quizzes assume but never test.

items.stem: What should the law be on marijuana for adults 21 and older?
items.scope: Recreational use, not medical. Driving while impaired stays illegal under every option.
items.context: About half the states allow adults to buy it legally. Federal law still bans it.
options: Legal to grow and sell, regulated like alcohol
Legal to have small amounts, but not sold in stores
Legal only for medical use with a doctor's recommendation
Illegal, with fines but no jail for small amounts
Illegal, with jail possible for having it

facts.claim: 24 states plus DC have legalized adult-use cannabis; it remains a federally controlled substance
facts.source: National Conference of State Legislatures; Controlled Substances Act
facts.note: Check federal rescheduling status (Schedule III process begun 2024; executive action Dec 2025).

items.stem: In places where marijuana is now legal, what should happen to people's past convictions for having small amounts?
items.scope: Convictions for possession only, not for selling or violence.
options: Clear them automatically
Clear them if the person applies
Keep them on record

items.stem: What should happen to adults caught with a small amount of a drug like cocaine or heroin for their own use?
items.scope: Personal use only. Selling drugs is a separate matter.
options: Nothing; it should be legal and regulated, like alcohol
A civil fine or a referral to treatment, not a crime
A crime, but treatment instead of jail for first offenses
A crime, with jail possible even for first offenses

items.stem: Should psilocybin, the drug in "magic mushrooms", be legal for adults?
options: Legal for any adult
Legal only in supervised settings, like a licensed center
Legal only as a prescribed treatment, if approved as a medicine
Illegal

items.stem: Should cities be allowed to run sites where people can use drugs they bring, with staff present to prevent overdose deaths?
items.scope: Staff would not provide drugs. They would offer treatment referrals.
options: Yes, and the federal government should help fund them
Yes, if the city chooses, without federal funding
No; they encourage drug use and should be illegal

items.stem: What should the law be on betting on sports through phone apps?
options: Legal everywhere, with few limits
Legal where states choose, with limits on advertising and bet sizes
Legal only in person at casinos and licensed locations, not on phones
Illegal

items.stem: What should the law be when one adult pays another adult for sex?
items.scope: Consenting adults only. Trafficking and anything involving minors stay serious crimes under every option.
options: No criminal penalties for either person
Legal, but only in licensed and regulated businesses, as in some Nevada counties
Illegal to pay for sex, but not to sell it
Illegal for both people, as in most states

items.stem: What should the law be on sexually explicit videos and images of adults?
items.scope: Content made by consenting adults. Content involving minors is always a serious crime.
options: Legal, with no special limits
Legal, but websites must verify that viewers are adults
Legal, but banned from most websites and sold only through restricted channels
Illegal to make or sell

items.stem: Should doctors be allowed to prescribe medicine that a dying adult can choose to take to end their life?
items.scope: Think of an adult who is mentally capable and expected to die within 6 months. Other situations come next.
items.context: About a dozen states and Washington, DC allow this.
options: Yes, with a short waiting period
Yes, with strict safeguards, such as two doctors' approval and a longer wait
No

facts.claim: Medical aid in dying is authorized in about 11-12 jurisdictions including DC (statute or court ruling)
facts.source: Death with Dignity National Center; state statutes

items.stem: Under the rules you chose, should these adults also be able to get this medicine?
options: Should be allowed
Should not be allowed

cases.text: Adults with an incurable illness causing severe suffering, who are not expected to die within 6 months
Adults whose only condition is a severe mental illness that has not responded to treatment
Adults with early dementia who ask for it in advance, for when the disease is advanced

items.subtopic: Public-health paternalism (sin taxes / helmet and seatbelt laws)
items.stem: Should government put extra taxes on unhealthy products to discourage people from using them?
items.scope: Taxes beyond the normal sales tax.
options: No extra taxes to discourage use; adults should make their own choices
Only on tobacco and alcohol, as today
Yes, on sugary drinks and junk food as well as tobacco and alcohol

items.subtopic: Public-health paternalism (sin taxes / helmet and seatbelt laws)
items.stem: Should adults be required by law to wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle?
options: No; adults should decide for themselves
Only riders under 21 or without health insurance
Yes, all riders
